questions.text: What distinguishes Layer 5 (Agents) from Layers 1 to 4?

options.text: Agents work only with images and audio.
You define the goal, and the agent plans and executes the steps needed to reach it.
Agents run without any internet connection.
Agents are the only layer widely available to teachers today.

questions.explanation: In Layers 1 to 4 the teacher drives, giving one instruction after another. With agents you define the destination and the AI plans the route itself.

questions.text: The six-layer framework in this lesson is an official technical classification of AI systems.
questions.explanation: The lesson states explicitly that this is not an official technical classification but a didactic framework — a mental map of what AI can and cannot do.

questions.text: According to the layer map, which layers are described as already widely available?
questions.explanation: The layer map marks Layers 1 and 2 as widely available, while computer-using AI and agents are listed as emerging and agent systems as being in early development.

questions.text: What does the lesson say happens to the teacher's role as AI becomes more capable?

options.text: It becomes less important, because AI takes over more of the work.
It becomes more important — setting goals, providing context, overseeing and judging.
It stays exactly the same at every layer.
It shifts entirely to technical maintenance of the tools.

questions.explanation: The lesson argues the teacher's role becomes more central, not less: as AI gains autonomy, the quality of the goal you set and the review you give the output matter enormously.
